translations.literal: Regional Commander Shuang Lai pressed forward vigorously, climbed the wall by ladder, and Jinshou coordinated the support.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Shuang Lai pressed forward vigorously, climbed the wall by ladder, and Jinshou coordinated the support.

sentences.zh: 兵不聽命，雙來以無援負創退，尋歿於軍，自此不敢力攻，而賊時由瓜洲窺伺來援，屢卻之。

translations.literal: The troops would not obey orders; Shuang Lai, lacking support, withdrew wounded and soon died in camp. From then on they dared not press the attack hard, while the bandits from time to time spied from Guazhou and came to relieve the city—they were repeatedly driven back.
translations.idiomatic: The troops would not obey orders; Shuang Lai, lacking support, withdrew wounded and soon died in camp. From then on they dared not press the attack hard, while the rebels from time to time spied from Guazhou and came to relieve the city—they were repeatedly driven back.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賊陷儀徵，兩路同時來犯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the bandits took Yizheng and came to attack on two routes at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the rebels took Yizheng and came to attack on two routes at once.

sentences.zh: 參將馮景尼守楊子橋，先潰，諸軍多失利。

translations.literal: Regimental Commander Feng Jingni defended Yangzi Bridge but collapsed first; many of the armies suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental Commander Feng Jingni defended Yangzi Bridge but collapsed first; many of the armies suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 城賊擁輜重突出趨瓜洲，琦善、金綬不能截擊，並坐褫職留軍。

translations.literal: The city bandits, laden with baggage, broke out and rushed toward Guazhou; Qishan and Jinshou could not intercept them and were both stripped of office but kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: The city rebels, laden with baggage, broke out and rushed toward Guazhou; Qishan and Jinshou could not intercept them and were both stripped of office but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 揚州雖復，賊久踞瓜洲。

translations.literal: Although Yangzhou was recovered, the bandits long held Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Although Yangzhou was recovered, the rebels long held Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 四年春，琦善卒於軍，金綬暫署關防。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year Qishan died in camp and Jinshou temporarily held the official seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year Qishan died in camp and Jinshou temporarily held the official seal.

sentences.zh: 托明阿至，偕金綬進攻瓜洲，毀賊砲台。

translations.literal: Tuo Ming'a arrived and, together with Jinshou, advanced to attack Guazhou and destroyed the bandits' batteries.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo Ming'a arrived and, together with Jinshou, advanced to attack Guazhou and destroyed the rebels' batteries.

sentences.zh: 尋攻新橋賊壘，金綬之侄能義及游擊海明殞於陣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they attacked the bandit stockades at Xinqiao; Jinshou's nephew Nengyi and Battalion Commander Haiming were killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they attacked the rebel stockades at Xinqiao; Jinshou's nephew Nengyi and Battalion Commander Haiming were killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 江北軍多疲玩，金綬年老，文宗以其謹願，姑容之。

translations.literal: The army north of the Yangzi was largely slack and negligent; Jinshou was old, and Emperor Wenzong, because he was cautious and compliant, for the time being tolerated him.
translations.idiomatic: The army north of the Yangzi was largely slack and negligent; Jinshou was old, and Emperor Wenzong, because he was cautious and compliant, for the time being tolerated him.

sentences.zh: 閱時輒報小捷，屢以虛飾被斥。

translations.literal: From time to time he reported minor victories and was repeatedly rebuked for false embellishment.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time he reported minor victories and was repeatedly rebuked for false embellishment.

sentences.zh: 至托明阿兵潰土橋，金綬及雷以諴駐萬福橋，望風而走。

translations.literal: When Tuo Ming'a's army collapsed at Tuqiao, Jinshou and Lei Yixian were encamped at Wanfu Bridge and fled at the mere sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuo Ming'a's army collapsed at Tuqiao, Jinshou and Lei Yixian were encamped at Wanfu Bridge and fled at the mere sight of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 事後飾辭自辨，又奏隨同克復揚州，為德興阿論劾，應治罪，金綬已先歿於軍矣。

translations.literal: Afterward he embellished his words in self-defense and also memorialized that he had joined in recovering Yangzhou; De Xing'a memorialized in impeachment and he should have been punished, but Jinshou had already died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he embellished his account in self-defense and also memorialized that he had joined in recovering Yangzhou; De Xing'a memorialized in impeachment and he should have been punished, but Jinshou had already died in camp.

sentences.zh: 德興阿，喬佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人，黑龍江駐防。

translations.literal: De Xing'a, of the Gioro clan, was a man of the Plain Yellow Banner of the Manchus, garrisoned in Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a, of the Gioro clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner and was garrisoned in Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 道光末，由駐京前鋒授藍翎侍衛、乾清門行走，累擢頭等侍衛。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daoguang reign, from a vanguard stationed in the capital he was appointed blue-feather bodyguard and attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and was repeatedly promoted to first-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daoguang reign, from a vanguard stationed in the capital he was appointed blue-feather bodyguard and attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and was repeatedly promoted to first-class bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 以善​​騎射受文宗知，曾手擒奔馬，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Because he was skilled in horsemanship and archery he won Emperor Wenzong's notice; he once seized a runaway horse with his own hands and was granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was skilled in horsemanship and archery he won Emperor Wenzong's notice; he once seized a runaway horse with his own hands and was granted the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，命率黑龍江兵赴琦善軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was ordered to lead Heilongjiang troops to Qishan's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he was ordered to lead Heilongjiang troops to Qishan's army.

sentences.zh: 三年，從攻揚州，屯蔣家廟，為通儀徵要路，城賊竄出，奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed in attacking Yangzhou and encamped at Jiangjiamiao, a critical route to Yizheng; city bandits broke out and he fought hard and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed in attacking Yangzhou and encamped at Jiangjiamiao, a critical route to Yizheng; city rebels broke out and he fought hard and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 瓜洲援賊進踞虹橋，與守備毛三元夾擊於三汊河。

translations.literal: Relief bandits from Guazhou advanced and seized Hongqiao; together with Garrison Commander Mao Sanyuan he attacked them from both sides at Sanhe River.
translations.idiomatic: Relief rebels from Guazhou advanced and seized Hongqiao; together with Garrison Commander Mao Sanyuan he attacked them from both sides at Sanhe River.

sentences.zh: 德興阿單騎陷陣，射殪其酋，大破賊，加副都統銜。

translations.literal: De Xing'a alone rode into the enemy lines, shot and killed their chieftain, inflicted a great defeat on the bandits, and was given the rank of vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a alone rode into the enemy lines, shot and killed their chieftain, inflicted a great defeat on the rebels, and was given the rank of vice commander.

sentences.zh: 別賊破儀徵，分兩路來犯。

translations.literal: Other bandits took Yizheng and came to attack on two routes.
translations.idiomatic: Other rebels took Yizheng and came to attack on two routes.

sentences.zh: 德興阿急趨東石人頭，毀賊浮橋。

translations.literal: De Xing'a hurried to Dongshirentou and destroyed the bandits' pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a hurried to Dongshirentou and destroyed the rebels' pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 而瓜洲賊又進築土城於河西，偪三汊河，與儀徵賊相犄角。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Guazhou bandits again advanced and built an earthen wall west of the river, pressing on Sanhe River and forming a pincer with the Yizheng bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Guazhou rebels again advanced and built an earthen wall west of the river, pressing on Sanhe River and forming a pincer with the Yizheng rebels.

sentences.zh: 德興阿偕總兵瞿騰龍渡河毀賊營，賊乃不能西進。

translations.literal: De Xing'a together with Regional Commander Qu Tenglong crossed the river and destroyed the bandit camps, and the bandits then could not advance west.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a together with Regional Commander Qu Tenglong crossed the river and destroyed the rebel camps, and the rebels then could not advance west.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，賊棄揚州城退踞瓜洲，官軍進复儀徵，授正白旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: That winter the bandits abandoned Yangzhou city and withdrew to hold Guazhou; the government army advanced and recovered Yizheng, and he was appointed vice commander of the Han Chinese Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebels abandoned Yangzhou city and withdrew to hold Guazhou; the government army advanced and recovered Yizheng, and he was appointed vice commander of the Han Chinese Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 四年，偕瞿騰龍進攻瓜洲，騰龍深入，為賊所襲，殞於陣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he joined Qu Tenglong in advancing to attack Guazhou; Tenglong went in deep, was attacked by the bandits, and was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined Qu Tenglong in advancing to attack Guazhou; Tenglong went in deep, was attacked by the rebels, and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 德興阿率勁騎馳援，賊敗走，軍賴以全，賜號博奇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: De Xing'a led elite cavalry in hurried relief; the bandits were defeated and fled, and the army was saved thereby; he was granted the title Boqi Batūru.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a led elite cavalry in hurried relief; the rebels were defeated and fled, and the army was saved thereby; he was granted the title Boqi Batūru.

sentences.zh: 尋复敗賊三汊河，賊埋地雷誘官軍，德興阿偵知，揮軍繞路而前，賊伏壘不出，遂分軍兩路夾攻，斬馘過當，奪獲大砲地雷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again defeated the bandits at Sanhe River; the bandits buried land mines to lure the government army, but De Xing'a detected this, led his army by a detour, and when the bandits lay hidden in their fort and would not come out, he divided his forces into two routes and attacked from both sides, killing more than the usual count and capturing great guns and land mines.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he again defeated the rebels at Sanhe River; the rebels buried land mines to lure the government army, but De Xing'a detected this, led his army by a detour, and when the rebels lay hidden in their fort and would not come out, he divided his forces into two routes and attacked from both sides, killing more than the usual count and capturing great guns and land mines.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，晉御前侍衛。

translations.literal: When victory was reported he was promoted to imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported he was promoted to imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 五年，迭攻瓜洲賊壘，又截擊竄賊於虹橋、八江口等處，皆獲勝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he repeatedly attacked the Guazhou bandit stockades and again intercepted fleeing bandits at Hongqiao, Bajiangkou, and other places, winning victory in each case.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he repeatedly attacked the Guazhou rebel stockades and again intercepted fleeing rebels at Hongqiao, Bajiangkou, and other places, winning victory in each case.

sentences.zh: 六年，托明阿兵敗於土橋，揚州复陷，諸軍渙散，獨德興阿軍未動。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Tuo Ming'a's army was defeated at Tuqiao, Yangzhou again fell, and the various armies scattered; only De Xing'a's army did not break.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Tuo Ming'a's army was defeated at Tuqiao, Yangzhou again fell, and the various armies scattered; only De Xing'a's army held firm.

sentences.zh: 詔黜托明阿，以德興阿為欽差大臣，加都統銜。

translations.literal: An edict removed Tuo Ming'a and made De Xing'a imperial commissioner, giving him the rank of lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Tuo Ming'a and made De Xing'a imperial commissioner, giving him the rank of lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 敗賊薛家樓，進規郡城。

translations.literal: He defeated the bandits at Xuejialou and advanced to invest the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels at Xuejialou and advanced to invest the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 賊萬人迎敵，德興阿身先士卒，斬賊酋一，諸軍乘之，賊大潰，乘勝复揚州。

translations.literal: Ten thousand bandits came out to meet them; De Xing'a led from the front, beheaded one bandit chieftain, the various armies pressed the advantage, the bandits collapsed in great disorder, and taking victory in hand they recovered Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand rebels came out to meet them; De Xing'a led from the front, beheaded one rebel chieftain, the various armies pressed the advantage, the rebels collapsed in great disorder, and taking victory in hand they recovered Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 同時江浦、浦口並為賊踞，令總兵武慶攻克之。

translations.literal: At the same time Jiangpu and Pukou were both seized by bandits; he ordered Regional Commander Wu Qing to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Jiangpu and Pukou were both seized by rebels; he ordered Regional Commander Wu Qing to capture them.

sentences.zh: 德興阿戰功素為江北諸軍冠，惟不曉漢文，命少詹事翁同書為幫辦。

translations.literal: De Xing'a's battle merits had long been foremost among the armies north of the Yangzi, but because he did not understand written Chinese, Junior Tutor Weng Tongshu was appointed to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a's battle merits had long been foremost among the armies north of the Yangzi, but because he did not understand written Chinese, Junior Tutor Weng Tongshu was appointed to assist him.

sentences.zh: 添調新兵，軍聲稍振，進規瓜洲。

translations.literal: Fresh troops were added and transferred in; the army's reputation revived somewhat, and he advanced to invest Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh troops were added and transferred in; the army's reputation revived somewhat, and he advanced to invest Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，參將富明阿破賊於土橋、四里鋪，水師又擊沉賊船，斬偽將軍陳磊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Regimental Commander Fu Ming'a defeated the bandits at Tuqiao and Sili Pu; the naval force again sank bandit boats and beheaded the false general Chen Lei.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Regimental Commander Fu Ming'a defeated the rebels at Tuqiao and Sili Pu; the naval force again sank rebel boats and beheaded the false general Chen Lei.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，合水陸諸軍進攻，毀賊艦及砲台。

translations.literal: That summer the combined land and naval forces advanced to attack and destroyed the bandit ships and batteries.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the combined land and naval forces advanced to attack and destroyed the rebel ships and batteries.

sentences.zh: 德興阿親督戰，更番進逼，至十一月，大破之，复瓜洲。

translations.literal: De Xing'a personally supervised the fighting and pressed forward in relays; by the eleventh month he inflicted a great defeat and recovered Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: De Xing'a personally supervised the fighting and pressed forward in relays; by the eleventh month he inflicted a great defeat and recovered Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 賊負嵎歷四年，至是始克。

translations.literal: The bandits had relied on difficult terrain for four years; only at this point were they finally taken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had relied on difficult terrain for four years; only at this point were they finally taken.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉調度有方，賜雙眼花翎，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: An edict praised his effective command, granted him the double-eyed peacock feather, and gave him the hereditary office of commandant of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his effective command, granted him the double-eyed peacock feather, and gave him the hereditary office of commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逼金山，剿平新河口、龍王廟等處餘匪。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of victory he pressed on Jinshan and suppressed the remaining bandits at Xinhekou, Longwangmiao, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Taking advantage of victory he pressed on Jinshan and suppressed the remaining bandits at Xinhekou, Longwangmiao, and other places.

sentences.zh: 江南軍亦同日克鎮江，專力進攻江寧。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan army also captured Zhenjiang on the same day and devoted its full strength to attacking Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan army also captured Zhenjiang on the same day and devoted its full strength to attacking Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 八年春，德興阿進軍江浦，獲勝。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year De Xing'a advanced to Jiangpu and won victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year De Xing'a advanced to Jiangpu and won victory.

sentences.zh: 江寧賊勢日蹙，悍黨陳玉成等由安徽糾眾來援，德興阿兵敗於浦口，退保六合，褫雙眼花翎，革職留任。

translations.literal: The Jiangning bandits' position grew tighter by the day; fierce leaders such as Chen Yucheng gathered followers from Anhui to come to their relief; De Xing'a's army was defeated at Pukou, withdrew to defend Liuhe, was stripped of the double-eyed peacock feather, and was removed from office but kept in post.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangning rebels' position grew tighter by the day; fierce leaders such as Chen Yucheng gathered followers from Anhui to come to their relief; De Xing'a's army was defeated at Pukou, withdrew to defend Liuhe, was stripped of the double-eyed peacock feather, and was removed from office but kept in post.

sentences.zh: 賊連陷江浦、天長、儀徵，德興阿不能救，揚州亦陷，褫世職。

translations.literal: The bandits in succession took Jiangpu, Tianchang, and Yizheng; De Xing'a could not save them, Yangzhou also fell, and his hereditary office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in succession took Jiangpu, Tianchang, and Yizheng; De Xing'a could not save them, Yangzhou also fell, and his hereditary office was stripped.

sentences.zh: 尋張國樑率兵渡江复揚州，而德興阿擁兵邵伯，觀望不前，嚴旨斥責。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zhang Guoliang led troops across the river and recovered Yangzhou, while De Xing'a held his army at Shaobo, watching without advancing; a stern edict rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhang Guoliang led troops across the river and recovered Yangzhou, while De Xing'a held his army at Shaobo, watching without advancing; a stern edict rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 溫紹原守六合歷數年，為江北屏蔽，至是亦以援絕被陷，紹原死之。

translations.literal: Wen Shaoyuan had defended Liuhe for several years as a shield for the north bank; at this point he too was taken when relief was cut off, and Shaoyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Shaoyuan had defended Liuhe for several years as a shield for the north bank; at this point he too was taken when relief was cut off, and Shaoyuan died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 翌日而張國樑馳至，已無及。

translations.literal: The next day Zhang Guoliang hurried there, but it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhang Guoliang hurried there, but it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 國樑以江寧軍事急，移軍渡江，詔責德興阿規复六合，軍已不振，迄無功。

translations.literal: Guoliang, because Jiangning military affairs were urgent, moved his army across the river; an edict charged De Xing'a to plan the recovery of Liuhe, but the army's spirit was already broken and in the end there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang, because Jiangning military affairs were urgent, moved his army across the river; an edict charged De Xing'a to plan the recovery of Liuhe, but the army's spirit was already broken and in the end there was no success.

sentences.zh: 何桂清疏劾：「德興阿秉性粗率，初賴翁同書相助，得克瓜洲。

translations.literal: He Guiqing submitted a memorial in impeachment: 'De Xing'a is by nature coarse and rash; at first he relied on Weng Tongshu's assistance to capture Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Guiqing submitted a memorial in impeachment: 'De Xing'a is by nature coarse and rash; at first he relied on Weng Tongshu's assistance to capture Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 自同書調任安徽巡撫去後，左右無人，毫無謀略，貽誤軍事。」

translations.literal: Since Tongshu was transferred to serve as governor of Anhui, he has had no one at his side, possesses no strategy whatsoever, and has caused military failure.'
translations.idiomatic: Since Tongshu was transferred to serve as governor of Anhui, he has had no one at his side, possesses no strategy whatsoever, and has caused military failure.'

sentences.zh: 和春亦劾其舉動乖謬，難以圖功。

translations.literal: He Chun also impeached him, saying his actions were perverse and erratic and success was hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun also impeached him, saying his actions were perverse and erratic and success was hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 文宗猶念其前勞，未遽加譴，九年，以圍攻六合久不下，革任召還。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong still remembered his earlier service and did not immediately punish him; in the ninth year, because the siege of Liuhe long remained uncompleted, he was removed from office and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong still remembered his earlier service and did not immediately punish him; in the ninth year, because the siege of Liuhe long remained uncompleted, he was removed from office and recalled.

sentences.zh: 自此江北不置帥，軍務統歸和春節制。

translations.literal: From then on no commander-in-chief was appointed north of the Yangzi; military affairs were uniformly placed under He Chun's control.
translations.idiomatic: From then on no commander-in-chief was appointed north of the Yangzi; military affairs were uniformly placed under He Chun's control.

sentences.zh: 尋予六品頂戴，交僧格林沁差遣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was given the sixth-rank official's button and placed under Sengge Rinchen's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was given the sixth-rank official's button and placed under Sengge Rinchen's orders.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署密雲副都統。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he served as acting vice commander at Miyun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he served as acting vice commander at Miyun.

sentences.zh: 同治初，授西安右翼副都統，留辦山西防務，又移駐陝西同、朝一帶防剿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi he was appointed vice commander of the right wing at Xi'an, remained to manage Shanxi defense, and was again transferred to garrison the Tong and Chao region of Shaanxi for defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tongzhi he was appointed vice commander of the right wing at Xi'an, remained to manage Shanxi defense, and was again transferred to garrison the Tong and Chao region of Shaanxi for defense and suppression.

sentences.zh: 五年，充塔爾巴哈台參贊大臣，授正紅旗漢軍副都統，幫辦新疆北路軍務。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as assistant commissioner at Tarbagatai, was appointed vice commander of the Han Chinese Plain Red Banner, and assisted in military affairs on the northern route in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he served as assistant commissioner at Tarbagatai, was appointed vice commander of the Han Chinese Plain Red Banner, and assisted in military affairs on the northern route in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 六年，丁母憂回旗。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when his mother died, he returned to his banner in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when his mother died, he returned to his banner in mourning.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，依都統例賜卹，諡威恪。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; posthumous honors were granted according to the precedent for lieutenant generals, and he was given the posthumous title Weike.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died; posthumous honors were granted according to the precedent for lieutenant generals, and he was given the posthumous title Weike.

sentences.zh: 論曰：勝保初以直諫稱。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Sheng Bao was at first famed for blunt remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Sheng Bao was at first famed for blunt remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 及出治軍，膽略機警，數著功績。

translations.literal: When he went out to command armies he was bold, resourceful, and alert, and repeatedly achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: When he went out to command armies he was bold, resourceful, and alert, and repeatedly achieved merit.

sentences.zh: 然負氣凌人，雖僧格林沁不相下。

translations.literal: Yet he was overbearing by temperament and would yield to no one, not even Sengge Rinchen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was overbearing by temperament and would yield to no one, not even Sengge Rinchen.

sentences.zh: 自餘疆臣共事，無不齟《齒吾》互劾。

translations.literal: With the other frontier officials with whom he served, none failed to clash and mutually impeach one another.
translations.idiomatic: With the other frontier officials with whom he served, none failed to clash and mutually impeach one another.

sentences.zh: 文宗嚴馭之，屢躓屢起，蓋惜其才也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong strictly controlled him; he stumbled repeatedly yet was repeatedly restored—presumably because the emperor valued his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong strictly controlled him; he stumbled repeatedly yet was repeatedly restored—presumably because the emperor valued his talent.

sentences.zh: 始終以客軍辦賊，無自練之兵，無治餉之權；

translations.literal: He always dealt with bandits as a guest army, without troops he had trained himself and without authority over supplies;
translations.idiomatic: He always dealt with bandits as a guest army, without troops he had trained himself and without authority over supplies;

sentences.zh: 撫用悍寇而紊紀律，濫收廢員而通賄賂，又縱淫侈不自檢束。

translations.literal: he pacified and employed fierce bandits and thereby disrupted discipline, indiscriminately took in dismissed officials and accepted bribes, and again indulged in excess without restraining himself.
translations.idiomatic: he pacified and employed fierce bandits and thereby disrupted discipline, indiscriminately took in dismissed officials and accepted bribes, and again indulged in excess without restraining himself.

sentences.zh: 卒因袒庇苗沛霖，與楚軍不相能，朝廷苦心調和而不之喻，遂致獲罪，功過固莫掩也。

translations.literal: In the end, because he shielded Miao Peilin and could not get along with the Chu army, and the court painstakingly sought reconciliation without making him understand, he finally incurred guilt—merits and faults alike cannot be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, because he shielded Miao Peilin and could not get along with the Hunan army, and the court painstakingly sought reconciliation without making him understand, he finally incurred guilt—merits and faults alike cannot be concealed.

sentences.zh: 托明阿、德興阿皆戰將，非獨當一面之才，負乘僨事，宜哉。

translations.literal: Tuo Ming'a and De Xing'a were both fighting generals, not men of talent to hold a front alone; that they bore unsuitable burdens and ruined affairs is only fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo Ming'a and De Xing'a were both fighting generals, not men of talent to hold a front alone; that they bore unsuitable burdens and ruined affairs is only fitting.

sentences.zh: 斯又不足與勝保並論矣。

translations.literal: These again are not worth mentioning in the same breath as Sheng Bao.
translations.idiomatic: They again are not worth mentioning in the same breath as Sheng Bao.
